draft.title: Salts in water and soil
card: Water and soil contain dissolved salts. Many are minerals that come from rocks, such as calcium, magnesium and sodium salts.
Heavy metals such as lead, mercury and cadmium can also get into water and soil. Mining, industry and old pipes are common sources.
A salt dissolved in water splits into ions that can move. More dissolved ions means the water carries electric current better.
Electrical conductivity measures how well a sample conducts electricity. A higher reading means more dissolved ions, so the sample is saltier.
draft.remember: More dissolved ions means higher conductivity, which means a saltier sample.

a.q: Why does a higher electrical conductivity show that a water sample is saltier?
opts: There are more dissolved ions to carry current
There are more undissolved solids settled at the bottom
The water molecules themselves carry more current
The sample contains more heavy metals than minerals
a.why: Dissolved salts form mobile ions, and these carry current through the water. More ions means a higher reading. Heavy metals add ions too, but conductivity does not tell which ions are present.
a.clue: Think about what moves to carry the current in the solution.

b.q: Farmer Sam tests water from two dams. Dam A has a conductivity reading twice that of Dam B. What can Sam conclude?
opts: Dam A has more dissolved ions than Dam B
Dam A has more lead than Dam B
Dam A has less dissolved salt than Dam B
Dam A has more mineral salts but no heavy metals
b.why: A higher reading means more dissolved ions, so Dam A is saltier. Conductivity cannot show which ions are present, so Sam cannot say the extra ions are lead, or that no heavy metals are there.
b.clue: Conductivity counts ions but does not name them.

a.best: There are more dissolved ions to carry current

b.best: Dam A has more dissolved ions than Dam B
